A traditional setting for hosting guests
Oct 2026 • Business
I was in Hanoi on a business trip and was taken to Phung Thanh for a meal with several older guests. I really liked the traditional décor. The furniture, tableware and overall design have a distinctly old-fashioned Vietnamese feel, which makes the restaurant look quite formal and suitable for hosting important guests. The food focuses on traditional Northern Vietnamese flavors. My favorite was the honey-roasted chicken, which was fragrant and had a nice hint of lime leaf. It reminded me of the kind of home-cooked meals I used to have years ago. The staff were polite and attentive, which made the older guests feel comfortable and respected. Prices are higher than at casual local restaurants, but considering the setting and service, I think it's a suitable choice for business meals and special occasions.

A quiet corner to escape the office for lunch
Sep 2026 • Solo
Work had been pretty stressful, so I decided to bring my laptop here for lunch and take a break from the office. I chose a table near the fish pond, where the greenery and sound of running water made it easy to relax for a while. I ordered a simple lunch set. The food was satisfying, and the fried rice had a nice texture without being too dry. The only issue was that several staff members were gathered near the entrance, so it took a few calls before someone noticed when I wanted to order another drink. Overall, if you want somewhere to have lunch alone, clear your head and get a little work done, this is a decent option.

A casual get-together before our Northern trip
Sep 2026 • Friends
A few of us from Saigon were visiting Hanoi and a friend recommended this place, so we decided to stop by for some food and drinks before heading off to explore the northern provinces. The restaurant is surrounded by bamboo and greenery, which felt quite different from the places we usually visit in the South. We ended up taking quite a few photos. We ordered a few dishes to share, including shrimp paste rolls and fried tofu. The shrimp rolls were quite good, but the tofu was softer than expected and wasn't very crispy. The dipping sauce was also fairly mild. Still, the outdoor atmosphere was pleasant, and sitting around with friends for a few drinks made for a nice afternoon.

A quiet dinner for our anniversary
Sep 2026 • Friends
We came here to celebrate our third anniversary because we had heard that the restaurant had a cool and romantic atmosphere. The red lanterns and light mist around the entrance looked quite charming in the evening. The food arrived hot and was nicely presented, although as someone from Central Vietnam, I found the seasoning a little too mild for my taste. I prefer stronger, spicier flavors, so some of the dishes felt a bit bland. The eel wrapped in pork caul fat was tender, but the flavor wasn't really to our taste either. On the positive side, the quiet setting, warm lighting and friendly service made it a comfortable place for the two of us to sit and talk.

A weekend meal with the kids
Sep 2026 • Family
We have two energetic kids, so on weekends we usually look for somewhere spacious with plenty of greenery where they can look around and explore. The kids really enjoyed the large fish pond and the water features here. They were so interested in everything around them that they barely asked for their phones, which was a nice change. We ordered a few family-style dishes, and the grilled river shrimp was the kids' favorite. They kept asking us to give them more. The staff were also very patient and helpful with the children. The prices are slightly higher than some other family restaurants, but considering the clean surroundings and comfortable space, I think it's reasonable.

A quiet setting for a business meeting
Sep 2026 • Business
Work has been quite hectic lately, so I booked a private room at Phung Thanh to meet with a business partner. The décor has a strong Northern Vietnamese countryside feel, and the private room was quiet enough for a proper business conversation. The appetizers and shrimp paste rolls were neatly presented and looked appealing. The flavors were decent, although nothing particularly memorable for me. My biggest issue was the Wi-Fi in the room, which stopped working just when I needed to open some documents. It was quite inconvenient during a work meeting. Hopefully, the restaurant can fix this soon. Otherwise, it's a fairly suitable place for meeting clients when you need some privacy.

A quick meal on a rainy day
Sep 2026 • Solo
It had been raining heavily in Hanoi all day, so I stopped here for something to eat rather than dealing with the flooded streets for too long. The restaurant has lots of greenery, a fish pond and the sound of running water, which made it feel much more relaxing than outside. I ordered the honey-roasted chicken with a bowl of steamed rice. The chicken was well marinated, with crispy skin and tender meat inside. Even though I was dining alone, the staff served me quickly and didn't make me feel overlooked. I sat facing the fish pond, listened to some Trịnh music and enjoyed a quiet meal. The prices aren't cheap, but considering the central location, I thought they were reasonable.

A nice spot for hanging out and taking photos
Sep 2026 • Friends
A few of us decided to try this restaurant after hearing that it had lots of nice photo spots. It really does have plenty of greenery, lanterns and little countryside-style corners, so we had quite a lot of fun taking photos. We were hungry, so we ordered a hotpot and some fried rice. The fried rice was nicely separated and had a good texture, and the price was pretty reasonable for students. The food overall was enjoyable, and the young staff were friendly and enthusiastic. The only annoying thing was that the Wi-Fi in our private room kept cutting out, so we couldn't upload our photos right away. Other than that, it was a fun place to go with a group, especially since the bill was quite manageable when split between everyone.

A relaxed evening date
Sep 2026 • Friends
We were looking for somewhere with a nice atmosphere for a Friday night and happened to find this place on TikTok, so we decided to give it a try. The restaurant has plenty of lanterns, greenery and the sound of running water, which makes it quite relaxing for a date. We ordered the chicken and red-date hotpot and some grilled river shrimp. The flavors were fairly light and subtle, not as sweet or strongly seasoned as some dishes we are used to in southern Vietnam. The staff were friendly, although it was sometimes difficult to get their attention because we were sitting in a slightly hidden corner. There was also some live music that evening, which made the atmosphere even nicer. Overall, a decent place for a change of scenery on the weekend.

A nostalgic space in the middle of the city
Sep 2026 • Family
We took advantage of the cool early-autumn weather and brought the grandparents to Phung Thanh for a family meal. The garden was really pleasant, with green bamboo, flowing water and a much quieter atmosphere than the busy streets outside. Since Mid-Autumn Festival is coming, the restaurant also had a few decorations inspired by the Vietnamese countryside, which added a nice touch. We ordered several Northern Vietnamese dishes, and my husband especially liked the eel wrapped in pork caul fat because the meat was tender and easy to eat. The restaurant was quite busy that day, so the service was a little slow and we had to remind them a couple of times about the tea. Still, sitting together and chatting in such a peaceful setting was worth it. We will probably come back with the family around the Mid-Autumn Festival.

A great culinary heritage experience – a refined city service
Jun 2026 • Friends
If you are looking for a place not only to eat a delicious meal, but also to touch the spirit of Vietnamese culture, Phuang Qing is the perfect destination. I had a really full and impressive evening here.
 A unique cultural heritage:
As soon as I walked through the door, I seemed to be separated from the bullshit of the street to return to a space full of memories. The presentation here is extremely refined, honouring the beauty of Vietnam’s architecture and heritage through every detail – from walls, lamps to decorative artifacts. The space is cosy, luxurious but still retains the charm, close.
 Vietnamese food is higher:
The dishes at the Temple are truly a feast for both taste and vision. The taste of traditional Vietnamese dishes is fully preserved but is presented and combines extremely creative ingredients. Each meal is carefully cared for, tastes well and carries the identity of the region.
 Professional and warm service:
The biggest plus that makes a meal perfect is the staff. The servants were very polite, knowledgeable about the menu and dedicated to explaining the cultural story behind each dish. The thoughtfulness, subtlety but not too bullshit made me feel really appreciated.
